subject.title: fix: harden security and release integrity

question: Should registered callbacks remain public-network-only, or should ClickClack support explicitly trusted private destinations through a narrow configured policy?
rationale: Both choices are defensible security contracts, but the current unconditional rejection changes supported deployment behavior and cannot be resolved safely without project intent.

options.title: Allow explicit private targets
options.body: Keep public-only as the default and add a narrow host/CIDR allowlist or trusted-callback policy with DNS-pinning and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep public-only callbacks
options.body: Declare private callbacks unsupported and add clear upgrade documentation and actionable registration errors for affected installations.

options.title: Split callback hardening
options.body: Land unrelated security and release work separately while the callback trust contract is decided.

recommendation.title: Allow explicit private targets
recommendation.body: Keep public-only as the default and add a narrow host/CIDR allowlist or trusted-callback policy with DNS-pinning and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the self-assigned MEMBER driving the callback policy and the surrounding security work on this branch.
